{
  "message": "I got the full ENLIL virtual-spacecraft data for all 10 bodies, in both the CME and the ambient run, plus nine 3D time slices around the key dates. At 3I during the XMM window ENLIL gives a median n = 1.256 cm⁻³. That is about 1.2 times the 1.05 in Codex's cross-check. The speed matches.

**Working recipe.** A plain GET with a browser User-Agent:
`https://ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/ror/api/get_run_file.php?runnumber=Jan_Deca_120925_SH_1&filename=<name>`
- The full file list, with sizes and a `downloadable` flag, is at `/ror/results/run_files.php?runnumber=Jan_Deca_120925_SH_1&format=json`.
- The server often returns 500 Proxy Error. Retrying up to 12 times with 5–20 s backoff and checking each file against its listed size handled it; every file arrived at the right size.
- Native files: `evo.<body>.nc` (4 MB, netCDF-3, holds both runs).
- CCMC text files: `filename=ENLIL_at_<body>.txt` (6.8 MB). These are not in the listing, but the API serves them.
- The 1D-viewer POST does not work: whatever fields you send, it returns no plot and a "0.00 KB" pointdata link that gives a 500. The `/RoR_WWW/.../ENLIL_at_*.txt` path is a 404. `bnd.nc` is marked `downloadable:false`.

**Tidy CSVs** (`timeseries/enlil_<body>.csv` for the CME run, `enlil_<body>_ambient.csv` for the ambient run, 10 bodies each):
- 27,499 rows each, at ENLIL's native step of about 4 min, from 2025-10-01T00:00:41 to 2025-12-09T00:00:52.
- Columns: `utc, t_day, r_au, lat_deg, lon_deg (HEEQ+180, Earth at 180), lon_heeq_deg, vr_kms, vlon_kms, vlat_kms (+north), n_cm3, T_K, br_nT, blon_nT, blat_nT (+north), dp (CME tracer), bp (polarity tracer), nvr_cm2s`.
- Time is seconds since 2025-10-01T00 UTC; `t_day` is the 1D viewer's "days since run start" axis. Latitude is heliographic, relative to the solar equator.
- Density is n = ρ / 1.67239e-27 kg, which is CCMC's own conversion.
- The raw magnetic field is stored without its polarity, so physical B = sign(BP) × (B1, B2, B3).
- Against CCMC's text files, every column agrees to 5e-6 relative. One exception: the text files' B_lat is southward-positive (not sign-flipped, although their V_lat is), so my `blat_nT` is exactly minus their B_lat. Their line-1 header also has the E_lat and E_lon columns swapped; the `#` header on line 8 has the right order.

**3I/ATLAS, XMM window 12-03T12:04 to 12-04T10:12** (353 steps, CME run; ambient differs by <0.1%). Position: r = 1.875 AU, latitude −6.46°, HEEQ longitude 75°.

| Quantity | Median | Min | Max |
|---|---|---|---|
| n (cm⁻³) | 1.256 | 1.206 | 1.610 |
| V_r (km/s) | 406.6 | 405.2 | 412.7 |
| \|V\| (km/s) | 406.6 | | |
| n·V_r (cm⁻² s⁻¹) | 5.11e7 | 4.97e7 | 6.52e7 |
| T (K) | 3.28e4 | 3.05e4 | 3.70e4 |
| \|B\| (nT) | 2.0 | | |

No CME material reaches 3I in the window (tracer about 1e-32). A compression arrives on Dec 5 (n up to about 3, T up to 1.1e5 K), then fast wind at about 630 km/s on Dec 6–7.

**Comparison with Codex.** The |V| agrees (406.6 vs 406.7). N and flux are both lower than mine by the same factor of 1.196 (1.05 vs 1.256, 4.27e7 vs 5.11e7). Nowhere in the XMM window does my n drop below 1.206. Values near 1.05 only occur before the window (Dec 1–3), when V_r was 420–445 km/s. That pattern fits a density conversion of ρ/(about 1.2 m_p) on their side. CCMC's own `ENLIL_at_3I-Atlas.txt` N column agrees with my values.

**Earth and STEREO-A, Nov 20 – Dec 5 medians (CME run):**

| | n (cm⁻³) | V_r (km/s) | n·V_r (cm⁻² s⁻¹) | T (K) | \|B\| (nT) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Earth | 3.41 | 467 | 1.50e8 | 7.26e4 | 4.54 |
| STEREO-A (HEEQ lon +49.9°, about 25° from 3I) | 3.13 | 495 | 1.62e8 | 6.87e4 | 5.01 |

**3D data: yes.** I fetched nine full 3D slices `tim.NNNN.nc` (99.5 MB each, 896 MB total), both runs in each file, at:
- 11-25 00:04 (0220)
- 11-30 00:02 (0240)
- 12-03 00:01, 06:03, 12:01, 18:04 (0252–0255)
- 12-04 00:01, 06:03, 12:01 (0256–0258)

The arrays are shaped (run, longitude 90, colatitude 24, radius 576), in SI units. Slice NNNN is about 6×NNNN h after run start. To check orientation, I interpolated the slices at the positions of 3I, Earth and STEREO-A: density matches the timeseries to 4 digits, and V and T within 0.3% (2% for T at Earth). The 1.15 GB boundary file `bnd.nc` was not downloadable. I skipped the `fld.<body>.nc` files (149 MB each) and did not open them.

**Quick-look graphics.** I saved 92 files in `quicklook/` (244 MB), all at their listed sizes:
- Density and velocity frames at Nov 25, Nov 30, Dec 3 12h, Dec 4 00h and Dec 4 06h, in Earth-centered and STEREO-A-centered views.
- Each body's timeline plots, the J-maps, and the CME arrival-time timelines and tables.
- The `den3-earth` and `vel3-earth` animations.

I left out the other animations (about 2.4 GB); they are in the listing.

**QC plots** (density, V_r, n·V_r and T for Nov 15 – Dec 9, both runs, XMM window shaded): `qc_enlil_3i.png`, `qc_enlil_earth.png`, `qc_enlil_stereoa.png`. I looked at all three and they render cleanly.

The `test_pd.txt` and `run_metadata.json` at the top of ref/ccmc were there before I started; they are an HTML page and a 500 error page, and I left them alone.

Everything is in `/mnt/c/Users/cabot/OneDrive/Documents/Research/Cambridge/X3I/mhd_llm/claude/ref/ccmc/`:
- README.md
- qc_enlil_3i.png
- qc_enlil_earth.png
- qc_enlil_stereoa.png
- timeseries/ (the 20 CSVs, crosscheck_vs_ccmc_txt.json, summary_windows.json)
- raw/nc/ (evo files, grd.nc, ror_metadata.json)
- raw/txt/ (CCMC text files)
- raw/tim/ (3D slices, check_tim_vs_evo.json)
- raw/run_files.json
- quicklook/
- scripts/ (fetch.py, getfiles.py, build_csv.py, check_tim.py, qc_plot.py, summary.py, idl1d_post.py)"
}
